Monmouthshire borders Herefordshire..why: True: stated in the Monmouthshire article (a Welsh county on the English border).

notes: RBox revision of symmetry: flips a property that holds (bordering is mutual) to its opposite. Symmetry of 'borders' follows from no other tag, so there is no premise route back. The direct question and the propositional statement spell out asymmetry ('only ever holds in one direction between two places') because models misread the bare word. Instances are minor true pairs (Rutland/Leicestershire, Monmouthshire/Herefordshire) whose converses are not famous stored facts. Yes and no are balanced by phrasing: the first instance (and the cross-lingual queries) asks whether the fact rules out the converse (no, then yes), the second whether the converse follows (yes, then no). Near asks the same property of another geography relation. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge. Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
